newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebel leader gives diplomacy a chance, Mbeki.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel leader gives diplomacy a chance, Mbeki.

text.p: South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said rebel leader Laurent Kabila agreed on Friday to give diplomacy a chance to resolve Zaire's civil war until meeting President Mobutu Sese Seko on a ship next week.
After talks with rebel leader Kabila in Zaire's second city Lubumbashi, Mbeki told reporters: "Mr Kabila says he is committed to the peaceful resolution of the Zaire conflict."

"He is willing to give diplomacy a chance and our understanding is he will not proceed with the military campaign until after next week's meeting," said Mbeki before leaving Lubumbashi for Libreville, Gabon, for talks with Mobutu.

Mbeki said Kabila agreed to meet Mobutu on a South African navy ship next Wednesday for their second round of face-to-face talks. The South African deputy president said he assumed Mobutu would agree to attend.
"That's why I am going to Libreville now, to meet Mr Mobutu and offer him an invitation from (South African) President (Nelson) Mandela for him to come to the talks next week," Mbeki said.
Mobutu and Kabila met last Sunday on a South African navy ship off the coast of Congo for talks chaired by Mandela.
Kabila, leader of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, wants Mobutu to resign and hand over power to him. But Mobutu wants an interim authority before elections.

Mbeki's trip is part of a South African attempt to mediate a peaceful transition of power in Zaire. Kabila's rebels now control three quarters of the country and Mobutu has agreed in principle to step down after more than three decades in power.
Rebel "Foreign Minister" Bizima Karaha said in Lubumbashi earlier on Friday that the rebels hoped Mobutu would sign his letter of resignation at next Wednesday's meeting with Kabila.
Karaha rejected as "absolute nonsense" steps for the transition of power in Zaire proposed by Central African leaders and vowed to oust President Mobutu Sese Seko unless he resigned.
He told Reuters the only acceptable course was for Mobutu to hand over power directly to Kabila or he could wait in the capital Kinshasa for the rebels to arrive and "chase him away".
"We are determined to remove this man from power, and to remove everything that he represents," Karaha added.
Karaha accused the Central African presidents of "playing games and trying to protect Mobutu. But we cannot be fooled."

Central African leaders on Thursday urged Zaire's parliament to fill the post of speaker -- Mobutu's constitutional successor in the event of his death or incapacity -- so the transition of power was orderly.
Washington on Thursday renewed its call for Kabila and Mobutu to work out a transitional government to put Zaire on a path to democracy and avoid a bloodbath as rebels advanced.
